name: Microsoft Dynamics NAV
description: Microsoft Dynamics NAV on-premises over OData v4: query and update any published page or query web service — customers, items, sales orders, vendors — in one company. NavUserPassword or Windows basic auth against your own NAV service tier.
instructions:
**Publish the web services first.** NAV exposes nothing by default. In the NAV client open **Web Services** (page 810) and add a row per object you want to reach: Object Type `Page`, the object id, and a **Service Name** — that service name is the OData entity set name, not the page's caption. Tick Published. Common ones: page 21 → `Customer`, page 27 → `Vendor`, page 30 → `Item`, page 42 → `SalesOrder`.

**Then point the connector at one company.**
1. `NAV_BASE_URL` is the OData root of your service tier, e.g. `https://nav.example.com:7048/DynamicsNAV110/OData`. No trailing slash.
2. `NAV_COMPANY` is the company name exactly as NAV spells it, including spaces — `CRONUS Deutschland GmbH`. The adapter builds `.../OData/Company('<name>')`, so one connector serves one company; add a second connector for a second company.
3. `NAV_USERNAME` and `NAV_PASSWORD` are a NavUserPassword credential (or a Windows account, if the service tier is configured for NTLM).

**OData v4 vocabulary**: `$filter`, `$select`, `$top`, `$orderby`, `$expand`. String comparison is `Name eq 'Muster'` with single quotes; dates are bare (`Order_Date ge 2026-01-01`). NAV replaces spaces in field names with underscores, so *Order Date* is `Order_Date`.

**Updates need the row's etag.** OData v4 requires `If-Match` on a PATCH. `dynamics_nav_update_record` sends `If-Match: *`, which means 'update whichever version is current' — simple, and deliberately last-writer-wins. Read the row first if that matters.

**SOAP is being retired**, in Business Central from release wave 2026-2. OData is the path forward, which is why this adapter speaks it and not the older SOAP endpoint.

**Self-hosted, which is the thing to plan for.**
- On **AnythingMCP Cloud** the instance must be reachable from the public internet on a real hostname with a valid TLS certificate. A self-signed certificate will fail: the connector offers no trust-anything switch.
- On an internal host (`nav.intern`, `10.0.0.x`), self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add that host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard refuses the call before it is made.

tools.name: dynamics_nav_list_services
tools.description: List the published web services available on this company — the entity set names every other tool needs. Start here: NAV exposes nothing that has not been published by hand.

tools.name: dynamics_nav_query
tools.description: Query any published entity set with OData v4. The general-purpose read: pass the service name plus $filter, $select, $top and $orderby.

service.description: Published web service name, e.g. Customer, Item, SalesOrder.

filter.description: OData $filter expression, e.g. Country_Region_Code eq 'DE'. Field names use underscores for spaces.

select.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. No,Name,Balance_LCY.

orderby.description: Sort expression, e.g. `Name asc` or `Order_Date desc`.

expand.description: Navigation properties to expand inline, e.g. SalesOrderSalesLines.

tools.name: dynamics_nav_get_by_key
tools.description: Read one record by its OData key. NAV keys are often composite, so pass the key exactly as it appears in a list response's `@odata.id`.

service.description: Published web service name, e.g. Customer.

key.description: OData key literal, e.g. '10000' or Document_Type='Order',No='101005'.

tools.name: dynamics_nav_get_metadata
tools.description: Read the OData $metadata document: every published entity type, its properties and their data types. The authoritative field list when a $filter keeps failing.

tools.name: dynamics_nav_create_record
tools.description: Create a record in a published entity set. Writes to the live NAV company and triggers the page's own validation and business logic.

service.description: Published web service name, e.g. Customer.

record.description: Field values for the new record, keyed by OData field name, e.g. {"Name": "Muster GmbH", "Country_Region_Code": "DE"}.

tools.name: dynamics_nav_update_record
tools.description: Update one record by key. Sends If-Match: * — last writer wins — so read the row first if a concurrent edit would matter.

key.description: OData key literal of the record to update.

record.description: Field values to set, keyed by OData field name.
